pr_title: input/cursor: restore pointer position after emulating touch input
pr_body:
Fixes #1896.

---

Disclaimer: I have no touch device with which to test this patch. It *seems* correct by reading through it, but some real testing from someone who can would be helpful :)

issue_context.title: Pointer events are issued at the last touch position
issue_context.body:
1. Move cursor to position A
2. Touch position B
3. Click with mouse
4. Observe that the click event was sent to position B, though the cursor has not moved

---

Hi, I've tried the recent master with the basic touch support - one thing I've experienced on my touch laptop:

tapping on my touch screen and afterwards clicking the mouse pointer results in a click at the last position of the touch pointer, though the mouse pointer is visible on a different position.

I'm not able to look at the code, but wanted to mention this, it's a small thing and can easily be overseen

Thanks for your great work on sway !
comments: I am unable to reproduce this

If the mouse pointer moves before the click, the coordinates update and it works as one expects

But not if the cursor doesn't move - in that case a popup triggered by right-click opens at the touch position

ah, I was able to reproduce by moving during the touch, which generates `TOUCH_MOTION` events, which evidently are updating the pointer position. libinput debug for click-touch-click and click-touchmove-click [here](https://gist.github.com/edrex/988f95007c432a27811926cdb4d254cc).
On a touch screen `for_window [...] move position mouse|pointer|cursor` moves a new window to a mouse cursor instead of a touch point.

review_comments: This is a little misleading tbh. Why shouldn't we update the cursor position when emulating touch input?

When we're using touch input, the cursor image is hidden. Updating the cursor position when on a touch surface is rather useless due to multi-touch, so we don't -- but that makes it confusing when the user moves over a non-touch surface, where we currently _do_ update pointer state despite the cursor not being visible. I think we should be consistent in what we do, so that users have a good idea of where their pointer is even when it's hidden (referenced issue).

For reference, other OSes I've tried:

* In Chrome OS, on touch the real cursor is hidden, and only reappears (in its original position) the next time a touchpad event is received.

* In Windows 10, touch down hides the cursor, but does not move it. Touch _move_ moves the real cursor (while still hidden), *unless* there are currently multiple touch points active, in which case the cursor does not move. The cursor reappears on a touchpad event.

The proposed behaviour is most similar to that from Chrome OS.

>I think we should be consistent in what we do, so that users have a good idea of where their pointer is even when it's hidden

Agreed.

What I'd expect is:

- Hide the pointer when using touch on a client that supports touch
- Show the pointer when using touch on a client that doesn't support it (emulated input)
- Show the pointer once a mouse/touchpad on the same seat starts being used again

Wdyt?
Also, I thought we were sending a pointer leave event when hiding the cursor while sending touch input?

> Show the pointer when using touch on a client that doesn't support it 

Hmm, this sounds like it offloads understanding about touch/non-touch surfaces to the user (e.g. "why does my pointer show up in application X but not in Y?").

I'll admit that I'm a bit biased to "just doing what other OSes do" since they probably had a bunch of UX people think more about this than I have, but I'm not sure I see the value in doing this. The UX between apps that handle touch events and those that don't is homogenous on Windows/Chrome OS -- the cursor is hidden unconditionally.

> Also, I thought we were sending a pointer leave event when hiding the cursor while sending touch input?

Yes, this matches my understanding too.

`handle_touch_down` [calls `cursor_hide`](https://github.com/swaywm/sway/blob/master/sway/input/cursor.c#L419) which [calls `wlr_seat_pointer_notify_clear_focus`]( https://github.com/swaywm/sway/blob/master/sway/input/cursor.c#L230).

This will cause the `pointer_state.focused_client` to become `NULL`, so any calls to `wlr_seat_pointer_send_motion` will [short circuit](https://github.com/swaywm/wlroots/blob/122318a5d5605e272d888e9a8b00a17e26b571c4/types/seat/wlr_seat_pointer.c#L235).

However, during pointer emulation we end up calling `handle_pointer_motion`, which [re-enters the surface](https://github.com/swaywm/sway/blob/master/sway/input/seatop_default.c#L558) (possibly immediately after having exited it -- now that I'm writing this out this sounds like another "bug" that should be addressed separately, later: we should only leave the surface if the surface supports touch).

>this sounds like it offloads understanding about touch/non-touch surfaces to the user (e.g. "why does my pointer show up in application X but not in Y?")

Correct, but it might also be less confusing: e.g. "why does multi-touch doesn't work on this app?" or "why can't I scroll by moving my finger on my touchscreen on this app?".

And also it feels like this behaviour would be less of a pain to implement. :P

>The UX between apps that handle touch events and those that don't is homogenous on Windows/Chrome OS -- the cursor is hidden unconditionally.

Ah, didn't know that.

Ultimately, I don't feel that strongly about it, I'm fine either way. What I'm more interested in is a way to properly fix this bug. The hack in this PR doesn't feel right -- do you have an idea to make this less hacky?

>now that I'm writing this out this sounds like another "bug" that should be addressed separately, later: we should only leave the surface if the surface supports touch

Yeah, created https://github.com/swaywm/sway/issues/5510 to track it.
